title: saasaloy-lock.json — resolved module provenance
description: Machine-owned lock at a generated project's root: for every installed module, the registry source it came from, the ref requested, and the exact commit SHA resolved — so a re-install reproduces identical bytes. The npm-style lock to saasaloy.json's intent (build spec §2.11; ADR 0012). Integrity is the commit SHA itself; there is no separate integrity field. The optional `base` object records the template `saasaloy init` rendered, keyed by CLI version and template hash rather than a commit, because the base ships inside the CLI package (ADR 0032).

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor validation.

lockfileVersion.description: Lock format version; bumped only on a breaking shape change.

base.description: Provenance of the base template `init` rendered, or `update` adopted. Absent on a project scaffolded before the record existed; `saasaloy update` writes it.

name.description: The base app's name — saasaloy.json's `base` field (`web`).

cliVersion.description: The CLI version that rendered or adopted the base. A label beside the hash: `outdated` compares `templateHash`, and `update` refuses a downgrade when both sides are real semver.

templateHash.description: sha256 over the sorted (path, sha256) pairs of the template as shipped in the CLI package. Differs whenever any shipped template file differs.

modules.description: Module name → the source it was resolved from. Holds the full resolved graph (dependencies included), not just the top-level asks.

source.description: Registry source slug: `owner/repo` for a remote GitHub source, or `local` for a SAASALOY_REGISTRY_DIR checkout.

ref.description: The ref requested (branch/tag/SHA), or `local` for a local checkout.

resolved.description: The exact commit SHA the ref resolved to — the integrity anchor. `local` for a local checkout.

dependsOn.description: The module's declared dependencies, recorded so the resolved graph is self-describing.

conflictsWith.description: The module's declared `conflictsWith` list, recorded because descriptors aren't kept after install — this is what lets `add` refuse a conflicting module that goes in second.
